title: Low-voltage wiring and the certificate
why: We size the cables, earth the install, fit the protection, and issue the certificate of compliance against this before handover.

title: PV and battery on a building supply
why: We wire the rooftop PV or hybrid inverter as part of the building supply and sign it off with the low-voltage certificate.

title: Medium-voltage site intake
why: On a site with a medium-voltage intake or transformer we do not use the low-voltage board rules on that side.

title: Cable type and how we lay it
why: We pick the cable for the route, whether tray, duct or direct buried, before we order the drum.

title: Cable current rating
why: We derate the cable for how it is buried or bunched, and we do not use the free-air rating in a duct.

title: PV cable
why: On the array we use cable made for PV DC, not ordinary building wire.

title: PV connectors
why: We use matched DC connectors on the strings, and we do not leave a connector open to the weather.

title: Earthing and shock protection
why: Bond PV frames and battery and inverter cases to earth and fit the right earth leakage, because a bad earth can leave metal live without tripping.

title: Earth electrodes
why: We design and test the earth electrodes, and we do not take the reading while the soil is wet from rain.

title: Earth rods
why: We use earth rods and couplers made for an earthing system, and we do not drive scrap rod.

title: PV test sheets and handover pack
why: We fill in the inspection sheets and the system record on site and hand them over with the job.

title: PV string wiring and DC isolation
why: We set the string layout, the DC cable and the isolation before the modules go down.

title: Module type approval
why: We check the module datasheet for this qualification before we buy modules.

title: Module safety approval
why: We ask for the module safety certificate as well as the type approval before we place the order.

title: PV wiring inside the building
why: We install the PV supply so it meets the building wiring rules, not as a separate system with its own habits.

title: Inverter safety listing
why: We do not install a PV inverter that has no safety listing to this standard.

title: Inverter stops when the grid drops
why: We leave anti-islanding on and we open the grid breaker to confirm the inverter stops.

title: PV fuses
why: Where strings are paralleled we fit gPV fuses, and we do not use an AC fuse on the DC string.

title: Lithium cell safety
why: We look for this safety standard on the battery datasheet before we accept the pack.

title: Battery room and cabinet safety
why: We include ventilation, access and isolation of the battery room or cabinet in the install.

title: Battery system safety
why: We treat the battery, inverter and protection as one storage system, not a loose pack of cells.

title: Industrial battery charger
why: We use this for an industrial charger on a stationary battery, not as the standard for a lithium storage cabinet.

title: Grid connection of the inverter
why: We do not commission a grid-tied inverter until the utility has accepted the connection.

title: Small low-voltage grid connection
why: Before we order the inverter we confirm with the municipality or Eskom whether this site uses the simplified connection or the full one.

title: Supply voltage quality
why: When a site reports dips or flicker we describe them in the utility's terms, and we do not set our own limits.

title: Generation licence or registration
why: We ask which NERSA approval this plant needs before we run it in parallel with the grid.

title: Utility meter
why: We leave the municipal or Eskom meter in place, and we do not move or bypass it.

title: Circuit-breakers
why: We fit a breaker only within the current and voltage on its label, and a PV breaker has to be DC rated.

title: Isolators and switches
why: The DC isolator on a string or battery is a switch-disconnector rated for that DC voltage, not an AC isolator.

title: Built switchboard
why: A board we design and populate is checked as a complete assembly, not only as a box of listed parts.

title: Distribution transformer
why: On a site with an oil-filled distribution transformer we read the kVA, voltages and vector group on the nameplate before we connect the low-voltage board.

title: Enclosure dust and water rating
why: For an outdoor inverter or roof box we read both IP digits and match them to the site.

title: AC surge protection
why: We fit a surge protector on the AC supply and we bond it to the same earth as the board.

title: PV surge protection
why: We fit a DC surge protector on the PV side, and we do not use an AC surge protector there.

title: UPS rating
why: We check whether the client asked for a UPS or a battery inverter, because an off-grid inverter is not a UPS.

title: Lightning protection of the building
why: A roof with modules gets a lightning protection system bonded to the electrical earth, and the array frame alone is not that system.

title: Air terminals and down conductors
why: We install the air terminals, down conductors and earth of the lightning system to this part, together with SANS 10313.

title: Explosive areas
why: If a battery room, fuel store or genset area is a hazardous zone we do not put ordinary electrical gear in it.

title: Electrical work at a fuel site
why: At a fuel store or filling station we classify the zones and we do not put ordinary electrical gear in them.

title: Lock-out and the certificate
why: We lock out and prove the circuit is dead, and we do not sign a certificate for work we did not inspect.
